reason: Upheld as a light ops plan with small fixes. Its facts check out. poll.log header 2026-09-29T18:25:22Z has columns ...,publicScore,privateScore and every COMPLETE row ends ',<public>,' with the private field empty; exp89t 56669888 is still PENDING there. The stop sequence it relies on already exists: R41-A7 (uptest save final_0007Z, one read_selected, one submissions list, stop the poller), R43-A8, and R44-A5 (watchdog v2 first, then poller 37016 and the rest). So 'leave no poller running' adds nothing new. The only new element is 'the private read is one call on request, not a loop'. It is lighter than the rival R45-LH-3 (hourly LB downloads, up to ~12 calls) and follows the 28 Sep API-load rule. It is fail-soft: an empty private field just means asking again later. It costs 0 Kaggle calls tonight and does not touch finals, decision B, R1-R10 or the evening chain. VALUE is post-hoc learning only. The finals lock at 20:00Z, so it cannot change the result. Three gaps limit it. (1) lb_poll.py calls 'competitions submissions -v' with no --page-size. CLI 2.2.4 defaults to 20 per page (max 200), and the poll's oldest row is probe 27 (24 Sep), while the team has ~56 entries. One default call would miss older anchors. (2) A medal or rank answer needs the private LEADERBOARD (one download). The submissions list alone does not give it, and the user's first question will be the medal. (3) Scores show 3 decimals, while cap 6 / K / CI / DIS effects are ~0.001-0.002 each. Many private 'signs' will read 0, i.e. unresolved at display precision. The sign table must name its clean pairs in advance, not pick them after seeing the scores.
